newsitem.title: USA: Utd Dominion extends pump/valve deal trend.
newsitem.headline: Utd Dominion extends pump/valve deal trend.

text.p: United Dominion Industries Ltd has increased the rapid consolidation of undervalued pump and valve companies with its friendly takeover of Core Industries Inc and Imo Industries Inc, analysts said.
Dominion said it will acquire Core for $25 per share and Imo for $6 per share in two separate transactions together worth $770 million, including debt assumtion and costs.

With Core's fluid control and construction segment, which includes valves, and Imo's pump business, United will continue to de-emphasize its building products segment and grow its industrial products segment.

"The two transactions represent a milestone in our efforts to reshape United Dominion's business mix and enhance margins and profitability," chairman and chief executive William Holland said in a prepared statement.
Imo and Core together will add about $750 million to United Dominion's annual revenues, which last year were almost $1.9 billion.

Alexander Blanton, analyst with Ingalls & Snyder, said "There has been a lot of interest in valve and pump companies. The stocks have not performed well, in some cases because earnings growth has not been startling."
These companies typically do well late in the economic cycle, he said, when industrial companies expand production capacity with new plant construction.

"But there has not been a great deal of factory expansion because companies have been able to get more out of existing facilities. We have not gone through the late-cycle condition where people are building a lot of facilties. This has held down the results of companies supplying equipment," he said.

"So it seems there is recognition on the part of the buyers that values in these companies are depressed, and it is the right time to acquire before they hit their stride," he added. "It is a sign we are not close to the top of the (business) cycle."
United's purchases are the fourth and fifth fluid technology takeovers in two months.

The multi-billion dollar merger trend began April 21 when ITT Industries Inc announced its acquisition of Goulds Pumps Inc for $37 per share, or about $815 million, plus assumption of $119 million in debt.
The transaction grew ITT Industries into the world's largest fluid technology company with $2.1 billion in annual revenue, topping Japan-based Ebara Corp's $1.6 billion.
On May 6, Durco International Inc and BW/IP Inc said they would merge in a stock swap to create a company with a market capitalization of $1.2 billion.
Two weeks later, Tyco International Ltd announced a $1.2 billion stock swap to acquire Keystone International Inc .

In afternoon New York Stock Exchange trade, Imo shares where up 2-5/8 to 5-3/4, a leap of 84 percent, and Core stock added 1-7/16, or 6.2 percent, to 24-11/16. Showing the market's positive approach to the deal, United Dominion shares were off 3/16 at 25-3/8.
